asha: quick heads-up — I ran a randomized anchor-injection sweep against the new quant4-int model to repro the KV divergence we saw with long tails.
ben: nice. which test harness?
asha: `tests/kv/longtail_anchor_sweep.py` with seed range 1000-1020, window=16384, priming length variable (0..4096). command:
```
pytest tests/kv/longtail_anchor_sweep.py::test_randomized_anchors -q --seed 1005 --max-context 16384 --capture=no
```
carl: any config differences from the main prefill run? quant params / rotary scale?
asha: kept runtime flags identical except `--rotary-scale=1.02` for half the seeds (to emulate slight RoPE drift) and we toggled `--kv-prefill-warmup=0/1` in pairs. also ran int8 and int4 variants for comparison.
devon: results? short summary pls.
asha: summary: 6/21 seeds hit a token-shift divergence after ~6k tokens with int4; int8 only 1/21. pattern: divergence correlates with injected anchor tokens falling near shard boundary (mod 4096). toggling rotary-scale to 1.02 tripled repro probability.
ben: do you have example input+output diff for a repro?
asha: pasted one small repro excerpt below (trimmed):
```
-- prompt prefix --
<anchor>A_2987</anchor> [random long tail .. ~7k tokens] \n-- model A (baseline int8) continues: "...the response concludes with X"\n-- model B (int4, rotary=1.02) continues: "...the response concludes with Y"\n```
The divergence shows token insertion at pos 6123 and subsequent KV indices misaligned.
carl: sounds like a RoPE phase alignment issue where the anchor pushes the effective index mapping across a shard boundary. Did you dump KV indices?
asha: yes — grabbed `kv_index_snapshot` from both runs. baseline index sequence around 6120 was contiguous; repro run had a duplicated index entry (6122 repeated) and then an off-by-one shift onward.
devon: could this be a memcpy/padding bug in the compacted cache path for int4 blocks? we had similar symptoms with earlier tiling bug.
ben: plausible. also check prefill eviction code: when prefix hits exact boundary we may be doing an unsafe slice. @carl did you see any OOB logs?
carl: I scanned GPU logs — no OOMs, but saw a warning in the runtime about `kv_prefill_stride` rounding at 0x7fffae. attaching snippet: `WARN runtime: preffill stride rounding adjusted from 16 to 8 for alignment`
asha: that aligns. repro seeds had stride adjustment due to long-tail alignment and quant packing. I also repro'd locally with `--dump-kv-hex` and saw byte-level shift in the int4-packed buffer at the same offset.
devon: next steps: 1) add a hardened assert in prefill path to detect duplicate index entries; 2) add a fuzz test for randomized anchor insertion across shard boundaries for int4 packing; 3) try a small patch to prefer 16-byte alignment before packing.
ben: +1. also run cross-check with dynamic rotary scaling disabled to confirm scale is amplifier not root cause.
carl: I'll prepare a minimal repro harness (single-file) that reproduces the memcpy effect and open a draft PR for the assert.
asha: putting my logs and the failing seed list in the eval bucket: s3://redwood-qa/kv-longtail-repro/seed-1005-1020.tar.gz
asha: note: when I re-ran the same seeds under dedicated hardware (different memcpy implementation) the failure rate dropped to 1/21, so runtime memcpy variant matters.
devon: good signal that pack/unpack path on host matters. can we mitigate with a defensive path that avoids packing near boundary?
ben: try runtime flag `--avoid-compaction-near-boundary` as a quick experiment.
asha: did that for the failing seed and it prevented the divergence (single-shot). I'll add a short smoke test to the CI.
eval-bot: automated eval run complete: 21 seeds, int4 pack-edge test, result: 6 failures -> regression ticket created (#INFR-2147).
carl: thanks — I'll assign the ticket and link the minimal repro.
asha: TL;DR: root likely packing/alignment interacting with RoPE scaling + anchor placement; patch + fuzz tests recommended.
ben: perfect, please add the CI smoke and mark for postmortem after fix. :thumbsup:
